title: Compatible finite normal replacements of the stages of a Noetherian approximation
statement: Let S be a quasi-compact quasi-separated integral scheme with integrally closed stalks and let N be a Noetherian approximation of S [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois, def-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system]. Over the same index category N.I there exist a diagram X, a cone alpha from S to X, and a natural transformation p from X to N.D. The composite alpha followed by p is N.pi. Every p_i is finite, every alpha_i is dominant, and every X_i is integral with integrally closed stalks. No limit property of alpha is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0EZJ, proof of Lemma 58.31.9, paragraph constructing normal integral stages and compatible transition maps; Tags 035E, 035N, 035L and 0335

proof.text: Apply the single-stage universal finite normal replacement at each index. For an arrow i -> j, lift p_i followed by N.D.map through the universal property at j, using alpha_i and naturality of N.pi. Unique lifts give the identity and composition laws and both naturality equations. These define X, alpha and p; their components have the finite, dominant, integral and normal properties supplied by the stage lemma.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_normal_finite_stage_diagram {S : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace S]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] [IsIntegral S]
    (hS : ∀ x : S, IsIntegrallyClosed (S.presheaf.stalk x))
    (N : S.NoetherianApproximation) :
    ∃ (X : N.I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (α : (Functor.const N.I).obj S ⟶ X) (p : X ⟶ N.D),
      α ≫ p = N.π ∧
      (∀ i, IsFinite (p.app i)) ∧
      (∀ i, IsDominant (α.app i)) ∧
      (∀ i, IsIntegral (X.obj i) ∧
        ∀ x : X.obj i, IsIntegrallyClosed ((X.obj i).presheaf.stalk x))
